    delightkitr

    Small, purposeless decorative flourishes — “delighters” — in the tradition of modelmaking greebles: no function, kept anyway because they feel good. Companion to musickitr, themekitr, and showkitr.

    Grew out of an Artifact prototype, “A Part That Does Nothing” — an organic shape with no job except reacting to you. delightkitr is that idea generalized across three surfaces, each with its own implementation, sharing one visual language: traits (color, faceted-ness) that mutate a small, bounded amount at each “division” instead of being randomized outright, so a decoration never looks arbitrary.

    The three surfaces

    1. Interactive (inst/js/) — self-contained HTML/JS/CSS, canvas-based, zero external dependencies. For Quarto HTML docs, Shiny apps, standalone pages. Copy-paste a file, or drop it in via an R helper (htmltools::tags-style).
    2. Static (R/, via grid::xsplineGrob()) — generated SVG/PNG appliques and borders for Quarto PDF/Word reports and ggplot2 figures. xspline()’s native shape parameter is the same smooth-to-faceted blend the canvas version built by hand — no headless-browser render step needed. Scoped to page chrome (margins, dividers, covers), never inside a plot panel — decoration shouldn’t compete with the data encoding.
    3. LaTeX (inst/tikz/) — native TikZ macros for borders and frames, not a shared asset with the other two (TikZ needs to stay vector-scalable and tile correctly at any page size). Same visual language, separate implementation.

    Install 

    # devtools::install_github("DavidBrocker/delightkitr")
devtools::load_all()                                       # while developing

    Use 

    dk_specimen()                 # default stage, caps at 420px wide
dk_specimen(width = "300px")  # narrower, e.g. a sidebar or Shiny column

    Call it at the console and it opens in the RStudio Viewer (via htmltools::browsable()); print it in a Quarto/R Markdown chunk and it renders inline with no results='asis' needed; use it as Shiny UI directly. Safe to call more than once on the same page — each call generates its own unique element IDs and scopes its CSS to a wrapper class, so instances never collide with each other or the host page.

    Print ornaments

    Twelve ornament kinds, listed by dk_ornaments() and buildable by id with dk_ornament(). See them all in the gallery (source: docs/index.html, rebuilt with Rscript data-raw/build-gallery.R).

    Family Kinds
    Rules swelled_rule_grob(), fleuron_rule_grob(), swash_grob()
    Borders rinceau_grob(), greek_key_grob(), scallop_grob()
    Medallions compass_rose_grob(), guilloche_grob(), rosette_grob(), sunburst_grob()
    Corners corner_grob()
    Marks asterism_grob() (dinkus and asterism)

    Borders and swashes fit themselves to the box they are drawn in, so tiles stay square and the repeat count always fits exactly.

    dk_ornaments()                       # the catalogue
grid::grid.draw(dk_ornament("guilloche", seed = 3))

    Static ornaments are grid grobs, so they compose into base grid, ggplot2 (annotation_custom()), gt, and Quarto, and are built from geometry alone (no imported assets).

    grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(compass_rose_grob(points = 12))

# ggplot2 (keep the box square, e.g. with coord_fixed())
ggplot2::ggplot(mpg, ggplot2::aes(displ, hwy)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = "grey70") +
  ggplot2::annotation_custom(compass_rose_grob(n_ticks = 48),
                             xmin = 5.3, xmax = 7.1, ymin = 30, ymax = 44)

# gt: needs the 'gt' and 'svglite' packages
gt::gt(head(mtcars[, 1:4])) |>
  gt_ornament(compass_rose_grob(n_ticks = 48), where = "header")

# Quarto / R Markdown HTML, in a chunk with `#| output: asis`
cat(ornament_html(compass_rose_grob(points = 12), width = 1.2, height = 1.2))

    Rules and endcaps are wide, short ornaments: draw them in a box about 8 times wider than tall (e.g. 4 x 0.5 inches). A seed makes each one a little different — always the same for the same seed, and without touching your global RNG.

    grid::grid.draw(swelled_rule_grob(seed = 1, ends = "diamond"))
grid::grid.draw(fleuron_rule_grob(seed = 7, ends = "fleuron"))

# as a divider in a Quarto HTML doc (chunk option `#| output: asis`)
cat(ornament_html(fleuron_rule_grob(seed = 2), width = 5, height = 0.6))

    In ggplot2 and gt 

    library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()

# Frame the whole plot: border ornaments on any sides, flourishes in the corners
ornament_frame(p, top = "greek_key", bottom = "greek_key",
               left = "scallop", right = "scallop", corners = TRUE)

# Or border just the panel, as a layer (give the scales a little room)
p + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +
  panel_ornament(top = "scallop", bottom = "scallop", corners = TRUE)

# gt: an ornament above the title and another below the table
gt::gt(head(mtcars[, 1:4])) |>
  gt_ornament_frame(top = "swash", bottom = "fleuron_rule",
                    title = "Motor Trend cars")

    Border ornaments fit themselves to the length of each side, so a frame suits any plot shape. ornament_frame() returns a grob that prints like a plot and saves with ggsave(). The gt helpers produce HTML (Quarto, R Markdown, the Viewer), not PDF or Word output.

    ornament_svg() renders any ornament grob to an inline SVG string, so the same bridge works for gt, Quarto, htmltools::HTML(), and Shiny.

    Status

    Species #1 (dk_specimen(), the interactive mitosis specimen) is in — ported from the Artifact prototype, CSS rescoped off :root onto a .delightkitr-specimen wrapper, classes namespaced dk-, element IDs templated per-instance. The static surface has started: compass_rose_grob() plus the grob-to-HTML bridge (ornament_svg(), ornament_html(), gt_ornament()). Twelve ornament kinds are in, all with seeded variation, plus the gallery. Next: more kinds (chains, dentils, cartouches, tailpieces), then the TikZ side.

    Credits and inspiration

    The design principle of the print ornaments — small ornament kinds generated from geometry with seeded variation, rather than imported artwork — follows tikz-flora by wn-mitch (MIT licence; site), which in turn credits Kevin Raymond’s florilegium (MIT). delightkitr does not copy their code or constructions: the ornaments here are independently written in R/grid. Where a future ornament adapts a specific tikz-flora construction, it will be credited in its own documentation and the MIT notice reproduced.
